intro.author: Zechariah son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo (1:1), from a priestly family; many scholars think chapters 9–14 come from a later prophet or circle
intro.written: Chapters 1–8 are dated 520–518 BC; chapters 9–14 are undated, and their date is debated
intro.audience: Jews who had returned from Babylon to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple
intro.setting: Zechariah began preaching two months after Haggai, in the second year of the Persian king Darius I. The returned community was small, poor and discouraged, the temple half-built, and Judah only a minor province of a vast empire. Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 credit Zechariah and Haggai with getting the rebuilding finished.
intro.purpose: To call the people back to God, encourage them to finish the temple, and lift their eyes to God's future plan: a cleansed people, a coming king, and the Lord reigning over all the earth.
intro.bigIdea: 'Turn ye unto me... and I will turn unto you': God is returning to dwell with his people, and his King is coming.
